messages:
maria (infra): Heads up — after the kubelet 1.28.5 rollout in us-east1 we're seeing ~35% of the GPU warm-pool (dedicated-gpu-t2d) nodes flip to NotReady. Pods are Pending and the scheduler is repeatedly preempting tiny-gang jobs. Cost/throughput impact visible on the Dedicated dashboard. :eyes:
kevin.s: saw the same. node conditions show NetworkUnavailable + DiskPressure on a few. dmesg shows a nv_peer_mem complain and a couple kernel oops. I pulled a node dump: ```kubectl describe node gpu-us-east1-07 | sed -n '1,120p'``` — taints: gpu-reserved:NoSchedule, and kubelet eviction threshold triggered.
ashley: quick question — is this limited to the warm-pool or hitting provisioned instances too?
maria (infra): mostly warm-pool (autoscaler-managed warmpool IGs). A couple dedicated static hosts also affected but much lower rate. Provisioning isn't keeping up because the scheduler is shuffling pods around instead of letting autoscaler add nodes.
raj: that explains the spike in preemptions. scheduler logs show frequent preempt/rebind cycles for tiny-gang workloads. looks like the scheduler is trying to pack but getting hung on taints + ephemeral nic flaps.
kevin.s: grabbing kubelet logs now. suspecting the node kubelet lost network plugin (cni) briefly which marks NetworkUnavailable and then kube-proxy/statefulset sidecars try to reconnect => pod readiness flips.
ashley: for immediate mitigation, propose: cordon the 4 worst nodes in the warm pool, drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data, and let IG replace them (rolling). That avoids the scheduler doing expensive preempts.
maria (infra): agree. will coordinate. Also suggest we temporarily disable preemptions for tiny-gang queue in the scheduler policy (can toggle a feature flag) to stop the churn while nodes recycle.
raj: quick FYI — that will increase unit cost (more warm nodes alive) but will reduce token retries and tail-latency. Last hour cost for the customer pool jumped ~6% from retry churn.
kevin.s: commands I'm running: ```for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=warm-gpu -o name); do kubectl describe $n | egrep 'Taints:|Conditions:'; done``` and ```kubectl logs -n kube-system kubelet-gpu-us-east1-07 | tail -n 200 > /tmp/kubelet-07.log```
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0443 -> us-east1 GPU warm-pool degradation. Runbook: https://redwood-infra/runbooks/gpu-kubelet-rolling
ashley: I'm starting the cordon+drain on 3 nodes (gpu-us-east1-05, -07, -12) now. Doing one at a time, 5 min gap.
maria (infra): noted — once drained we'll mark them for a full kernel/driver reboot and reimage if checks fail. One ask: disable the scheduler preempt flag before the second drain. Kevin, can you flip it?
kevin.s: flipping preempt flag to false for tiny-gang queue. patch applied and reloaded scheduler. logs show preempt attempts falling to near-zero.
raj: updating autoscaler config: increase warm-pool min by +2 to absorb the immediate demand while reimage happens. Will revert once stable.
kevin.s: driver team confirmed a regression in 535.86 -> rolling driver restart should clear nv_peer_mem complaints. reimage script includes driver rollback to 535.65 if module errors found.
ashley: first node drained and rebooted. health checks passed post-reboot. bringing it back to the pool.
maria (infra): excellent. postmortem checklist: collect kubelet logs from drained nodes, scheduler trace for preemptions, autoscaler scaling events, and cost delta for the hour.
raj: I'll post a short blameless summary to incidents after we stabilize.
kevin.s: temporary mitigation succeeded; we're seeing Pending queue shrink and Dedicated throughput returning to normal. Will follow up with a PR to add a warmpool health probe to avoid autoscaler reusing flaky instances.
maria (infra): Thanks team. action items: (1) finish rolling reboots on the remaining 3 nodes, (2) rundriver rollback job on nodes with module errors, (3) add warmpool health probe + scheduler flag documented in runbook.
ashley: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: INC-2026-0443 status -> mitigated, monitoring.
